assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nitrogenase is the enzyme that makes biological nitrogen fixation possible, and its FeMo-cofactor is a unique metal cluster. The work unites genetics, crystallography, spectroscopy and kinetics to reach a physical-chemical account of multi-electron, proton-coupled catalysis, which is the kind of mechanism-in-living-systems chemistry I weigh most heavily. The field's importance is beyond dispute.
assessment.attribution: The decisive lines are structure (Rees, with Einsle's later high-resolution and carbide work), genetics and cofactor assembly (Dean, Ribbe), and mechanism and kinetics (Seefeldt, building on the Lowe-Thorneley framework). A three-person split of structure, genetics and mechanism is plausible but leaves out Einsle and Ribbe, so priority and allocation would need careful expert-report review.
assessment.maturity: Structures date from 1992 and have been refined and confirmed over decades, including the central carbide and the E4 state. Recognition is mature. The catalytic mechanism is still debated, which lowers the clarity of the final story somewhat.
uncertainties: Whether the mechanism of N2 reduction is settled well enough for a prize citation.
Allocation among five credited people when the limit is three, and whether the Lowe-Thorneley kinetic scheme predates the credited group.
Whether the prize should be framed as structure, genetics or mechanism.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Long-range electron transfer through proteins connects Marcus theory to biology through experiments in which donor-acceptor distance and the medium were varied. It supplies the physical basis for electron tunnelling in respiratory and photosynthetic chains, which is close to my own field. The conceptual clarity and generality are high.
assessment.attribution: Gray and Winkler are the clear experimental core, using ruthenium-modified proteins and tunnelling-pathway analysis. Related theory (Marcus, Beratan, Onuchic) lies partly outside the credited names and partly in earlier prizes. The two-person configuration is clean but the field includes others whose contributions could be questioned.
assessment.maturity: The work spans forty years and is thoroughly confirmed and textbook material. Recognition would be late rather than premature. The Marcus 1992 prize may have absorbed part of the conceptual credit.
uncertainties: How much of the credit is already covered by the 1992 prize for electron transfer theory.
Whether the experimental program is a discovery or a long line of work with distributed credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers makes diffraction-before-destruction possible and lets one record structures of radiation-sensitive proteins at room temperature. Time-resolved SFX can follow reactions on femtosecond to millisecond scales, and in 3D, which is what I value in methods that make dynamic mechanisms visible. Photosystem I and II and bacteriorhodopsin are examples.
assessment.attribution: Hajdu proposed and developed the underlying concept, Chapman led the 2011 proof-of-principle with Fromme's photosystem I nanocrystals, and Schlichting led much of the time-resolved and chemistry-focused work. Giving three places to four credible people is a real constraint, and a tripartite division of concept, demonstration and application is open to dispute.
assessment.maturity: The method is only a decade and a half old. The proof of principle is confirmed independently at several XFELs, but the broad record of new chemical mechanisms is still accumulating. It is promising but arguably early.
uncertainties: Whether the chemical discoveries enabled by SFX are broad enough yet.
Who among Hajdu, Chapman, Fromme and Schlichting is decisive.
Overlap with synchrotron serial crystallography credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Multidimensional NMR methods, including triple resonance, TROSY-type approaches and relaxation dispersion, allow structures and also dynamics of large biomolecules in solution to be determined. This reveals conformational exchange and invisible excited states relevant to catalysis and regulation. The effect on biochemical mechanism studies has been large.
assessment.attribution: Bax and Kay are the primary methodological authors, and Clore is a major structure and dynamics contributor. Wagner and Palmer have credible claims, and Wüthrich's 2002 prize already covers the NMR structure foundation, which complicates the credit story.
assessment.maturity: The methods are decades old, widely used and independently confirmed. Timing is mature, and arguably overdue, while an overlap with the 2002 prize reduces novelty.
uncertainties: Incremental advances over Wüthrich's earlier method may be judged as a line of work and not a single discovery.
Allocation among five credited people.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy-landscape theory with the folding funnel gave a physical, statistical-mechanics answer to Levinthal's paradox and has shaped understanding of folding kinetics and function. It is a physics-minded chemical principle. Fersht's experiments are the key empirical test.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central originators of funnel theory. Dill's hydrophobic-collapse framework is related but separate, and Fersht's phi-value analysis is the experimental counterpart. The credit is shared across theory and experiment, which makes a clean three-person split harder.
assessment.maturity: The framework has been confirmed over thirty years, but a fully predictive quantitative theory of folding is not established. The 2024 prize for structure prediction and design may have shifted the context for folding.
uncertainties: Whether the funnel picture counts as a discovery or an organizing concept.
The relationship to the 2024 prize for protein structure prediction.
Allocation between theory and experimental credit (Fersht).

assessment.nobel_worthiness: PROTACs and molecular glue degraders harness the ubiquitin-proteasome system to degrade chosen proteins, a chemical principle with clinical programs already underway. They create a new pharmacological mode, with a mechanistic base in induced proximity and ternary-complex chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated PROTACs; Ciulli contributed VHL ligands and structural ternary-complex work. Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim and Gray have claims, with Handa and Ito in the cereblon and thalidomide link. Credit is split between PROTAC and molecular-glue mechanisms.
assessment.maturity: The idea dates to 2001, but clinical validation is still emerging and mechanistic understanding of ternary complexes keeps evolving. A prize now would be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Clinical efficacy and long-term impact are not yet established.
Whether PROTAC and thalidomide-glue discoveries should be recognized together or separately.
Priority between Crews, Deshaies and Sakamoto.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy gives time-resolved structural information on vibrational coupling and dynamics of molecules, including water, peptides and proteins, on picosecond timescales. It is a physical method for following molecular dynamics, close to my own preferred approach of time-resolved spectroscopy.
assessment.attribution: Hamm and Zanni are authors of the foundational textbook and experiments; Tokmakoff has developed protein and water applications; Fleming and Mukamel developed key experimental and theoretical foundations. Allocation is hard with five credited people and several overlapping research groups.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature after more than twenty years. Its concrete scientific discoveries are spread out and no single result has an obvious impact beyond the field.
uncertainties: Whether impact beyond specialist physical chemistry is sufficient.
Splitting credit between theory (Mukamel) and experiment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The spliceosome work combines biochemistry and cryo-EM to reveal how a large RNA-protein machine catalyzes pre-mRNA splicing at the atomic level, a mechanism of central importance in biology. It fits a tradition of recognizing structural mechanism work for molecular machines.
assessment.attribution: Lührmann provided the biochemical and architectural foundation, and Shi and Stark provided major cryo-EM structures. Nagai and others with structural claims are not in the credited names, which complicates fairness. Prior contributions on splicing mechanism (Steitz, Cech-type ribozyme work) are also relevant.
assessment.maturity: Structures from 2015 onward have been independently reproduced and extended, but the chemical details of catalysis rest largely on analogy to group II introns. Timing is reasonable but this may be better suited to Physiology or Medicine.
uncertainties: Missing contributors (for example Nagai) who are not among the credited names.
Fit between the field and Chemistry versus Medicine.
Whether chemical catalytic mechanism is resolved in enough detail.
